issues.description: The problem statement (UML and description) requires a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int, but both the provided code examples and the solution implement and reference a method named computeMealCost(Meal). This name mismatch between the specification and the code artifacts can confuse students about which method name to implement and may lead to tests or instructor expectations failing.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either rename the method in the specification to computeMealCost(Meal): int (and update the UML and instructions) or rename the method in the solution/template to calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int. Ensure all examples (Main), UML, and tests use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute the net cost of a meal, but the solution implements this functionality under a different name (computeMealCost). This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual operation (compute total price of a Meal) creates confusion for students mapping the requirement to the implementation and may cause test or compilation mismatches if tests expect calculateTotalPrice.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name for the meal price calculation across all artifacts. Rename the solution method computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice (public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal)) or add a calculateTotalPrice wrapper that delegates to computeMealCost. Also update any Main or template references to call calculateTotalPrice so the implementation matches the problem statement/UML.
